## Reading Data from a File

Real clinical datasets live in files, not Python dictionaries. `pandas` can read CSV, Excel, JSON, and many other formats. We'll use our NHS readmission dataset:

::: {.callout-note}

The dataset is entirely synthetic — I generated it programmatically with Python (numpy and pandas) during our conversation, using:

Simulated distributions based on typical NHS inpatient population parameters (e.g. age ~Normal(62, 16), length of stay ~Exponential(4.5), HbA1c ~Normal(60, 18))
Clinically plausible missingness patterns (HbA1c missing in ~16% of patients, eGFR in ~9%)
A logistic outcome model where readmission probability depends on age, Charlson index, length of stay, prior ED attendances, eGFR, and IMD decile — consistent with the published literature on readmission predictors, but not derived from any real data

It does not come from any real NHS dataset, published repository, or external source. It was created purely to serve as a realistic teaching example.
:::

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("nhs_readmission.csv")

print(df.shape)
print(df.head())
```


::: {.callout-note}
## Column descriptions

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `patient_id` | Anonymous patient identifier |
| `age` | Age in years at admission |
| `sex` | M / F |
| `imd_decile` | Index of Multiple Deprivation (1 = most deprived, 10 = least) |
| `primary_diagnosis` | ICD-10 code for primary diagnosis |
| `charlson_index` | Charlson Comorbidity Index (0–37) |
| `hba1c` | Most recent HbA1c (mmol/mol) — missing if not tested |
| `egfr` | Most recent eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²) — missing if not tested |
| `bmi` | Body Mass Index (kg/m²) |
| `los_days` | Length of stay in days |
| `ed_prior_year` | ED attendances in previous 12 months |
| `readmitted_30d` | Readmitted within 30 days: Yes / No |
:::

### Dealing with common CSV issues

Real NHS data exports often have quirks:

```python
# Non-standard missing value markers
df = pd.read_csv("nhs_readmission.csv", na_values=[".", "N/A", "NULL", "UNKNOWN"])

# Specify date columns for correct parsing
df = pd.read_csv("nhs_readmission.csv", parse_dates=["admission_date"])

# Encoding issues (common with NHS system exports)
df = pd.read_csv("nhs_readmission.csv", encoding="latin1")
```

## Exploring the Dataset

After loading, always run a structured data quality check:

```python
# Shape: rows × columns
print(f"Dataset: {df.shape[0]} patients, {df.shape[1]} columns")

# Data types
print("\nData types:")
print(df.dtypes)

# Missing values per column
print("\nMissing values:")
print(df.isnull().sum())

# Summary statistics
print("\nSummary statistics:")
print(df.describe())
```

```

Data types:
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Clinical note: Why is data missing?
Missing `hba1c` (16% of patients) likely means the test was not ordered — common in surgical or trauma admissions. Missing `egfr` (9%) may mean no recent blood tests. In machine learning, "missing" can itself be an informative signal: patients without eGFR measurements may be less well-monitored. Always think about *why* data is absent before deciding how to handle it.
:::

## Querying Data

### `value_counts()` — Frequency tables

```python
# Outcome balance
print(df["readmitted_30d"].value_counts())
print(df["readmitted_30d"].value_counts(normalize=True).round(2))
```

```
readmitted_30d
No     3850
Yes    1150
Name: count, dtype: int64

readmitted_30d
No     0.77
Yes    0.23
Name: proportion, dtype: float64
```

We have a **class imbalance**: 77% not readmitted, 23% readmitted. We'll need to account for this when fitting models.

```python
# Top 10 primary diagnoses
print(df["primary_diagnosis"].value_counts().head(10))
```

```
primary_diagnosis
E11    842   # Type 2 diabetes
I10    631   # Hypertension
J44    518   # COPD
I50    487   # Heart failure
N18    342   # CKD
...
```

### `groupby()` — Aggregation by group

`groupby()` splits the dataset into groups and applies a function to each — the pandas equivalent of an Excel PivotTable.

```python
# Mean length of stay by readmission status
los_by_outcome = df.groupby("readmitted_30d")["los_days"].mean()
print(los_by_outcome)
```

```
readmitted_30d
No      3.8
Yes     7.2
Name: los_days, dtype: float64
```

```python
# Multiple statistics at once
df.groupby("readmitted_30d")[["age", "charlson_index", "los_days"]].agg(["mean", "median"]).round(1)
```

```
               age       charlson_index    los_days      
              mean median           mean median      mean median
readmitted_30d                                                  
No            62.1   63.0            1.8    2.0       3.8    3.0
Yes           70.4   71.0            3.4    3.0       7.2    6.0
```

Readmitted patients are on average 8 years older, have higher comorbidity burden, and stay nearly twice as long.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Exercise 4
1. How many unique values are in the `primary_diagnosis` column?  
   (*Hint*: `df["column"].nunique()`)
2. What is the mean HbA1c for readmitted vs non-readmitted patients?  
   (*Hint*: `df.groupby("readmitted_30d")["hba1c"].mean()`)
3. Which IMD decile has the highest readmission rate?  
   (*Hint*: `df.groupby("imd_decile")["readmitted_30d"].apply(lambda x: (x=="Yes").mean())`)
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## Answer (click to open)
```python
# 1.
print(df["primary_diagnosis"].nunique())

# 2.
print(df.groupby("readmitted_30d")["hba1c"].mean().round(1))

# 3.
readmit_by_imd = df.groupby("imd_decile")["readmitted_30d"].apply(
    lambda x: (x == "Yes").mean()
)
print(readmit_by_imd.sort_values(ascending=False))
# IMD decile 1 (most deprived) typically shows highest readmission rate
```
:::

## Creating New Columns

You can create derived columns by applying operations to existing ones:

```python
# Categorical age groups
df["age_group"] = pd.cut(
    df["age"],
    bins=[0, 18, 40, 65, 120],
    labels=["<18", "18–40", "41–65", ">65"],
    right=True
)
print(df["age_group"].value_counts())
```

```
age_group
>65      2341
41–65    1987
18–40     612
<18        60
Name: count, dtype: int64
```

```python
# Flag high-risk patients (Charlson ≥ 3 AND age > 65)
df["high_risk"] = (df["charlson_index"] >= 3) & (df["age"] > 65)
print(df["high_risk"].value_counts())
print(f"\nHigh-risk patients: {df['high_risk'].sum()} ({df['high_risk'].mean():.1%})")
```

```
high_risk
False    3841
True     1159
Name: count, dtype: int64

High-risk patients: 1159 (23.2%)
```
